original_question: Classify the continued fractions that correspond to the same cubic extension of the field of rational numbers Q.
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Problem 13 (V. Arnold): "Classify continued fractions that correspond to the same cubic extension of the field of rational numbers."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it keeps the operative verb "classify," the main object "continued fractions," and the field-theoretic condition of corresponding to the same cubic extension of Q. In fact, it is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of Problem 13.
missing_details: The paper poses this as an open problem, not as a theorem or conjecture.

The surrounding context is not arbitrary continued fractions in isolation, but geometric/multidimensional continued fractions attached to sails, specifically the algebraically periodic setting discussed just before Problem 13.

Nearby context in Section 3.1 case [A] supplies a hidden algebraic hypothesis: the relevant sails come from the totally real algebraic setting (integer matrix, irreducible characteristic polynomial over Q, all roots real).
The phrase "the same cubic extension" should be made explicit as: fix a cubic number field K/Q and classify the continued fractions associated with that fixed field.

The natural ambient equivalence notion in the paper is integer-lattice equivalence/integer congruence of the associated geometric objects; the draft does not say what counts as the same continued fraction for classification purposes.

Problem 13 sits inside the subsection on combinatorial structure of sails, so the intended classification is paper-internal and geometric, not a broad classification of all possible continued-fraction expansions of cubic irrationals by any method.
The paper immediately notes that the problem remains open even in the classical subcase of ordinary periodic continued fractions; this scope marker is absent from the draft.

There are no extra variables, operators, asymptotic quantifiers, degree parameters beyond "cubic," or conditions like homogeneity/nilpotency in the source statement; the missing content is contextual rather than symbolic.
refined_question: For a fixed cubic extension K/Q, classify—within the paper’s algebraically periodic geometric-continued-fraction framework (the algebraic sail setting of case [A], implicitly the totally real real-sail situation)—all continued fractions that correspond to K, up to the paper’s ambient integer-lattice equivalence of the associated sails.
justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 13 in Section 3.3, whose wording it almost reproduces. To make it stand-alone while staying as close as possible to the paper, the rewrite only adds the nearby hidden context that the paper is discussing algebraically periodic geometric/multidimensional continued fractions arising from sails in the algebraic case [A], and that the ambient notion of sameness throughout the paper is integer-lattice equivalence. I did not broaden the question to general cubic irrationals, arbitrary continued-fraction algorithms, or all field-theoretic parametrizations, because the paper itself states the problem narrowly and only adds the remark that it is open even for ordinary periodic continued fractions.
